effect_mechanism: Mangrove belts reduce coastal flooding by breaking waves and, more weakly, lowering surge water as it passes through the forest [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3]. Existing mangroves cut wave heights by 31% in a meta-analysis of field measurements [ev_frmg_nara16_1], and measured surge peaks fall by 5 to 50 centimetres per kilometre of mangrove [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1]. A global model finds that losing current mangroves would flood 28% more people each year [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1], and a Philippine model gives 24% more [ev_flood_hazard_wbphl17_1]. In India and Bangladesh, villages sheltered by existing mangrove forest took less salt water and flood water after super cyclones [ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7, ev_flood_hazard_akber18_7]. The avoided damage has been put in money terms: in Orissa mangroves protected houses worth USD 1218 per hectare of forest in a single cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and mangroves in front of sea dykes cut repair costs by 20–30% [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10]. Of restoration projects reviewed, 50% report better storm protection [ev_frmg_nara16_5]. In New Zealand, an existing mangrove forest about 1 km wide with no drainage channels lowered peak water by about 24 cm per km [ev_flood_hazard_montgomery18_1], and a global model of restoring all restorable mangroves in front of dikes finds about 140,000 fewer people (3%) affected by flooding each year [ev_flood_hazard_tiggeloven26_1].
conditionality: Most of this evidence describes existing forest, so it shows what keeping mangroves protects; that a planted belt will do the same is assumed [ev_frmg_nara16_1, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbphl17_1, ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7]. Surge and tidal water is lowered much less than waves [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3], and a World Bank Bangladesh model finds mangroves change total design water level by less than 4% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1]. In Indonesia, permeable brushwood dams that let mangroves return trapped about 0.5 m of sediment in four months while the coast kept eroding elsewhere [ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_1]. In Bangladesh, government mangrove planting on coastal mudflats is reported to have been very effective in building land, with rapid sediment build-up [ev_sediment_retention_becklange16_1].
